This second compound then targets Jurkat, a cell line often used in cancer research. The pathway implies that the isoflavone may act through a series of molecular interactions, ultimately influencing cellular processes in Jurkat cells. The evidence suggests a possible role for the isoflavone in modulating histone function, which could have implications for cellular behavior in Jurkat cells.
